standard_code: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: Learning About Our Environment
standard_text: Water in rivers and dams can be polluted with solids, chemicals and germs. Water is purified by settling, sieving, filtering, adding chemicals and boiling. Clean water is scarce in many places and must be saved. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 6, theme: Learning About Our Environment)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: Learning About Our Environment): separating mixtures, separation methods, water pollution, safe drinking water and conserving water. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Filtering removes solids; boiling kills germs.
key_sub: Water is scarce, so we must save it.
body_html:
How to think about it

Water from a river or dam may contain sand, leaves, chemicals and germs. It is purified in steps: settling (heavy solids sink), sieving and filtering (remove small solids), adding chemicals such as chlorine (kills germs) and boiling (kills germs at home).

Many communities in Nigeria, especially in the north, have limited clean water. We must not pollute rivers and should save water: close taps, fix leaks, reuse grey water and collect rainwater.

Example

Which step kills germs in water at home?

Heat it

Answer: boiling

Example

Muddy water is poured through a coffee filter. What is removed?

What is too big for the holes?

Answer: the mud (solids)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking clear water is always safe to drink.
  • Thinking filtering removes germs and dissolved salts.
  • Thinking water will never run out.

faq.a: Used water from washing that can be used again to water gardens.

faq.q: Why is chlorine added to tap water?
faq.a: It kills germs that cause diseases such as cholera.

items.q: Which method would you use to separate salt from salt water?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: What is distillation?
c: boiling a liquid and condensing the vapour to collect a pure liquid
items.e: Distillation separates liquids with different boiling points.

items.q: Which method gets salt back from salt water?
items.e: The water evaporates and leaves the salt.

items.q: Which would dissolve sugar fastest?
c: hot water, stirred, with fine sugar
cold water, not stirred, with sugar cubes
items.e: Heat, stirring and smaller pieces speed up dissolving.

items.q: Which method is best for separating pure water from orange juice?
items.e: Only the water boils off and is condensed.

items.q: Which method is best for separating iron filings and sand?
items.e: Iron is magnetic; sand is not.

items.q: What is a solute?
c: a solid that does not dissolve
the substance that does the dissolving
items.e: Sugar is the solute in sugar water.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate iron filings and sand?
items.e: Use using a magnet because iron is magnetic; sand is not.

items.q: Which of these could be separated by filtration?
c: ethanol from a mixture of ethanol and water
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate paperclips and marbles?
items.e: Use using a magnet because steel paperclips are magnetic; glass marbles are not.

items.q: Which of these could be separated by evaporation (crystallisation)?
c: the different dyes in a black ink
the colours in a food colouring
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which of these could be separated by chromatography?
c: the different dyes in a black ink
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate muddy water?
items.e: Use filtering because mud is made of insoluble bits.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate sea water (to get the salt)?
items.e: Use evaporating because salt is dissolved in sea water.

items.q: Which method is best for separating sugar from sugar solution?
items.e: Heat gently: the solvent evaporates and the solute remains.

items.q: Which method would you use to separate ethanol from a mixture of ethanol and water?
items.e: Choose the method from the properties of the substances.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate steel pins and sawdust?
items.e: Use using a magnet because steel is magnetic.

items.q: Which method is best for separating pure water from sea water?
items.e: Water boils, turns into vapour and is condensed back into a liquid.

items.q: Which is the best way to separate pebbles and soil?
items.e: Use sieving because pebbles are large.

items.q: Which method is best for separating salt from salt solution?
items.e: The water evaporates and leaves the salt behind.

items.q: A dry mixture contains gravel, iron filings and salt. Which part is separated out by evaporating the water (after adding water and filtering)?
items.e: The dissolved solid is left when the water evaporates.

items.q: A dry mixture contains salt, sand and steel paperclips. Which part is separated out by a magnet?
items.e: Only the magnetic metal is attracted.

items.q: A mixture contains sand, salt and iron filings. Why is water added and stirred before filtering?
c: so the salt dissolves and passes through the filter, leaving the sand
items.e: Only the dissolved salt goes through the filter paper.

items.q: A dry mixture contains chalk powder, salt and steel paperclips. Which part is separated out by filtering (after sieving, using a magnet and adding water)?
items.e: The insoluble solid is caught in the filter paper.

items.q: A dry mixture contains gravel, sand and sugar. Which part is separated out by filtering (after sieving, using a magnet and adding water)?
items.e: The insoluble solid is caught in the filter paper.

items.q: A dry mixture contains dried peas, sand and steel paperclips. Which part is separated out by a magnet?
items.e: Only the magnetic metal is attracted.

items.q: A dry mixture contains chalk powder, iron filings and sugar. Which part is separated out by evaporating the water (after adding water and filtering)?
items.e: The dissolved solid is left when the water evaporates.

items.q: A dry mixture contains chalk powder, pebbles and sugar. Which part is separated out by a sieve?
items.e: Only the big pieces are too large to pass through.

items.q: Tobi dissolves 20 g of salt in 200 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: A dry mixture contains gravel, salt and sand. Which part is separated out by a sieve?
items.e: Only the big pieces are too large to pass through.

items.q: A dry mixture contains pebbles, steel paperclips and sugar. Which part is separated out by evaporating the water (after adding water and filtering)?
items.e: The dissolved solid is left when the water evaporates.

items.q: A mixture contains sand, salt and iron filings. Which step comes last?
c: Use a magnet to remove the iron filings.
Add water and stir so the salt dissolves.
Evaporate the water to get the salt back.
items.e: Evaporating leaves the dissolved salt behind at the end.

items.q: A dry mixture contains iron filings, sand and sugar. Which part is separated out by evaporating the water (after adding water and filtering)?
items.e: The dissolved solid is left when the water evaporates.

items.q: A dry mixture contains chalk powder, dried peas and sugar. Which part is separated out by filtering (after sieving, using a magnet and adding water)?
items.e: The insoluble solid is caught in the filter paper.

items.q: Nkechi dissolves 15 g of salt in 50 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: Chioma dissolves 5 g of salt in 150 g of water, then evaporates all the water. About how much salt is left?
items.e: Evaporating removes only the water; all the salt is left.

items.q: A dry mixture contains iron filings, salt and sand. Which part is separated out by a magnet?
items.e: Only the magnetic metal is attracted.

items.q: A dry mixture contains sand, steel paperclips and sugar. Which part is separated out by evaporating the water (after adding water and filtering)?
items.e: The dissolved solid is left when the water evaporates.

items.q: A mixture contains sand, salt and iron filings. Which step is a good first step?
c: Evaporate the water to get the salt back.
Add water and stir so the salt dissolves.
Use a magnet to remove the iron filings.
items.e: Take out the magnetic iron first, while everything is dry.

items.q: Usman mixes 5 g of sand with 150 g of water, filters it and dries the sand. About how much sand is collected?
items.e: The sand does not dissolve, so all of it is caught by the filter.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by burning rubbish in the open?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the air.

items.q: What is permeability?
c: how easily water can flow through a material
items.e: Connected pores.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by litter left on a beach?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the land.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by rubbish thrown into a canal?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the water.

items.q: Why do some industries reuse cooling water?
c: to save water and reduce thermal pollution
to make water hotter for rivers
items.e: Recycling water saves resources.

items.q: Obinna observes: “Plastic bags blow into the ocean.” What impact can this have?
c: animals swallowing or getting tangled in plastic
warmer water with less oxygen for fish
air pollution and more carbon dioxide
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: Which indicator suggests a stream is healthy?
c: many mayfly and stonefly larvae living in it
lots of foam and a bad smell
items.e: Some insects need clean water.

items.q: What is non-point source pollution?
c: pollution from many spread-out places, like lawns and roads
items.e: It is harder to control.

items.q: Kelechi observes: “Fertiliser runs off farms into a river.” What impact can this have?
c: algae blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish
animals swallowing or getting tangled in plastic
air pollution and more carbon dioxide
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: What happens to water's volume when it freezes?
items.e: Ice is less dense.

items.q: What does a wastewater treatment plant do?
c: makes drinking water from the ocean
cleans used water from homes before it returns to lakes and rivers
items.e: Sewage must be treated.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by rubbish dumped in a forest?
items.e: The pollutant goes into the land.

items.q: Why is ocean water salty?
c: Rivers carry dissolved minerals from weathered rock into the sea, where water evaporates and leaves salt behind.
items.e: Dissolved load.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by aircraft taking off near homes?
items.e: Loud sounds disturb people and animals.

items.q: How do permeable pavers help water systems?
c: They add salt to the water.
They let rainwater soak into the ground instead of running off.
items.e: More infiltration recharges groundwater.

items.q: How do limestone caves form?
c: Slightly acidic groundwater dissolves the limestone.
items.e: Chemical weathering.

items.q: Which kind of pollution is caused by fireworks set off near a bird sanctuary?
items.e: Loud sounds disturb people and animals.

items.q: What does a water treatment plant do?
c: removes particles and germs to make water safe to drink
items.e: Steps include filtering and disinfecting.

items.q: Nonso observes: “Forests are cleared for new houses.” What impact can this have?
c: warmer water with less oxygen for fish
algae blooms that use up oxygen and kill fish
items.e: Human activities can change Earth's systems.

items.q: Why does warm water hold less life in a lake?
c: Warm water holds less dissolved oxygen.
items.e: Thermal pollution lowers oxygen.

items.q: What is a low-flow showerhead?
c: a showerhead that uses less water per minute
items.e: It saves water and the energy to heat it.

items.q: Does water have to boil to evaporate?
c: No. It evaporates at any temperature, just faster when warm.
items.e: Puddles dry without boiling.

items.q: Which action conserves water at home?
c: fixing leaky taps and taking shorter showers
running the tap while brushing teeth
washing a car with a running hose
items.e: Small changes save a lot of water.

items.q: What happens to water vapour when it cools?
items.e: Cooling causes condensation.

items.q: What is transpiration?
c: water leaving plant leaves as water vapour
items.e: Trees add lots of water vapour to the air.

items.q: Why should old medicines be returned to a pharmacy instead of flushed?
c: Treatment plants cannot remove all medicines, so they end up in lakes.
items.e: Take-back programmes protect water.

items.q: Which test result suggests water has a lot of pollution from fertiliser?
c: high levels of nitrates and phosphates
items.e: Nutrients feed algae blooms.

items.q: Why does a cold drink can get wet on the outside?
c: Water vapour in the air condenses on the cold surface.
items.e: Condensation.

items.q: Which part of the water cycle happens when a puddle dries up?
items.e: Liquid to gas.

items.q: What is a rain garden?
c: a planted dip that soaks up runoff from roofs and driveways
a garden that only grows in rain
items.e: Rain gardens reduce flooding and pollution.

items.q: What is water vapour?
items.e: We cannot see it.

items.q: Which household product is safest for the water system?
c: old medicine flushed down the toilet
motor oil poured on the driveway
a drain cleaner poured down the sink every day
items.e: Choose products that break down safely.

items.q: Which of these causes land pollution?
c: exhaust fumes from cars and buses
fireworks set off near a bird sanctuary
items.e: Rubbish dumped in a forest leads to land pollution.

items.q: Why are wetlands important to water systems?
c: They filter pollutants, store floodwater and recharge groundwater.
items.e: Protecting wetlands protects water.

items.q: Where is most of Earth's water?
items.e: About 97% of Earth's water is salty sea water.

items.q: Which is a source of water pollution?
c: fertiliser and manure washing off farm fields
items.e: Runoff carries nutrients and chemicals.

items.q: Which of these causes water pollution?
c: old furniture dumped at the back of a block of flats
items.e: Oil spilled from a ship leads to water pollution.

items.q: What does pH measure in water?
c: how acidic or basic the water is
items.e: Most aquatic life needs a pH near 7.

items.q: What is one way to reduce farm runoff?
c: plough right up to the stream
leave strips of plants (buffers) along streams
remove all trees by the stream
items.e: Plants trap soil and nutrients.

items.q: Which of these causes water pollution?
c: exhaust fumes from cars and buses
plastic bags left in a park
fireworks set off near a bird sanctuary
items.e: Rubbish thrown into a canal leads to water pollution.

items.q: Which of these is a way to save water?
c: taking a long bath every day
leaving the tap running while soaping hands
washing a few clothes in a full machine
items.e: Saving water means using only what we need.
